title: Operating Suite Maximum Surgery Allocation
real_world_story: A hospital has one sterile hybrid robotic operating room. Surgeons from various specialties have submitted N surgical booking requests for tomorrow. Each request i specifies a start minute s_i and finish minute f_i. Due to strict sterility protocols, only one surgery can occupy the suite at any moment. A surgery that finishes at minute T allows another surgery to commence immediately at minute T. Hospital management wants to perform as many procedures as possible.
problem_statement: Given N surgical requests with start time s_i and finish time f_i (where s_i < f_i), determine the maximum number of mutually compatible, non-overlapping surgical procedures that can be conducted in the single operating suite.
task: Calculate the maximum number of non-overlapping surgeries that can be scheduled.
input_format:
The first line contains a single integer N, the number of surgical requests.
The next N lines each contain two space-separated integers s_i and f_i, representing the start and finish times.
output_format: Print a single integer representing the maximum number of surgeries that can be scheduled.

examples.explanation: Surgeries sorted by finish time: [1, 4], [3, 5], [0, 6], [5, 7]. Selecting [1, 4] leaves next compatible surgery [5, 7]. Maximum scheduled surgeries = 2.
All three surgeries are contiguous with no overlapping interior time: surgery 1 finishes at 20, surgery 2 starts at 20 and finishes at 30, surgery 3 starts at 30. All 3 can be scheduled.

real_world_takeaway: Greedy activity selection (earliest deadline / finish time first) mathematically guarantees the maximum count of compatible events in a single resource.
